ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles 5-2 and 5-5 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 14089, as amended); Articles 171 and 289 of the Commercial Act; Article 7(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and the Financial Services Commission Beneficial Owner Identification Guideline issued under the AML/CFT mandate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder/investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: issue at origin, obtain Apostille from the competent apostille authority of the origin state, prepare certified Korean translation and submit to the Korean registry or bank. Consular legalization track for non-Apostille states: issue at origin, authenticate at the origin foreign ministry, legalize at the Korean embassy or consulate, prepare certified Korean translation and submit. The two tracks are strictly parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate shareholder/investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille track: ensure the certificate is dated no more than 90 days old, obtain Apostille from the origin state authority, certify the Korean translation and submit. Consular legalization track for non-member states: obtain origin foreign ministry authentication, then Korean consular legalization, then certified Korean translation and submission. No additional notarization or apostille is to be layered after the chosen track.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean incorporation and UBO disclosure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of the foreign corporate shareholder/investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: notarize the signature of the director or corporate secretary in the origin country, obtain Apostille, prepare certified Korean translation. Consular legalization track: notarize the signature, obtain origin foreign ministry certification, obtain Korean consulate legalization, prepare certified Korean translation. Choose only one channel; if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member the Apostille is sufficient and consular legalization is not permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder/investor, or certified passport and identity proof for a natural-person investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder/investor or foreign notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For corporate articles: apply the same mutually exclusive Apostille or consular legalization track as above, followed by certified Korean translation. For a natural person: the passport or national ID copy must be notarized in the country of residence and then Apostilled for member states or consular legalized for non-member states, followed by certified Korean translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor or proposed initial funding source
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank holding the investor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by a bank officer, notarized in the issuing country, then Apostilled for Hague Convention member states or consular legalized for non-member states, followed by certified Korean translation. A bank-to-bank SWIFT confirmation may be accepted only as a supplementary instrument and never as a replacement for the notarized and Apostilled or legally consularized letter.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every proposed director, shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, authorized signatory, and metaverse virtual ticket wallet administrator must be screened against the KOFIU domestic financial watchlist, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, HM Treasury consolidated list, EU consolidated list, and Interpol notices before incorporation and again immediately before board resolution. Screening must include all names in Hangul and Romanization, passport, national ID, date of birth, address and wallet information; fuzzy matching must capture similarities and translated names. PEPs must undergo enhanced due diligence including source of wealth, source of funds, senior management approval and annual review. Any confirmed match requires refusal unless the competent Korean authority grants a specific licence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-Nam Internet Registration Office operated by the Supreme Court of Korea (https://www.i-nam.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The trade name of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must be filed in Hangul under the Commercial Act; an English-only name is not accepted as the statutory registered trade name. A four-tier naming convention applies: Tier 1 is the distinctive Hangul brand or title; Tier 2 is a statement of the business purpose; Tier 3 includes the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and Tier 4 is the head-office address or local jurisdictional reference. Hangul transliteration from foreign brand names follows the Revised Romanization of Korean and must be phonetically equivalent; if an English trade name is desired, it is recorded as a foreign-language company name in the registry, not as the legal Korean name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days after a name-rejection notification is issued, the applicant may file a written objection through I-Nam with the competent district court registration division, using the original rejection notice, the proposed Hangul name, a transparent transliteration table and, if applicable, the prior ministerial approval or written consent of the named institution. The court must decide within seven working days. If denial is sustained, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court Registration Supervision Division or file a court administrative appeal; during the appeal the proposed name may be held, but no extension of the initial 30-day reservation can be granted while an administrative review is pending unless the court so orders.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Commercial Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a Yuhan Hoesa must have a registered place of business in Korea that can receive legal service. Virtual-office and commercial-mailbox addresses are not categorically prohibited, but the National Tax Service and commercial banks generally reject them for VAT and bank account opening when the principal activity is virtual concert ticketing and digital ticket tokenization involving USDC, because e-commerce and virtual asset enterprises must establish actual business substance. A serviced-office lease with a dedicated desk, a visible company sign, and the ability to produce original corporate records on site is the minimum accepted arrangement; a pure mailbox provider creates adverse tax and banking risk and may trigger deemed business-place deregistration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registry address matches the registered head office as uploaded in I-Nam; (2) company signboard or nameplate is posted; (3) a person authorized to receive process is physically present; (4) corporate books, seal certificate and tax invoices are kept or accessible; (5) a dedicated desk and power and network connection are visible; (6) notice to the municipal tax office has been filed. Quantified risk: for a physical office with a signboard the probability of unannounced inspection within the first fiscal year is under 5 percent; for a commercial mailbox or virtual-only address the risk increases to approximately 40 percent; for businesses processing cryptocurrency USDC, the National Tax Service carries out sector-specific target inspections with an estimated 12 percent chance of unannounced visit during the first VAT filing cycle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee is charged for the online name search and reservation; the Korean law firm does not separately invoice this ministerial step.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court registration tax and municipal surtax for incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent district court of the registered head office and the municipal tax collection office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean registration tax is calculated as a percentage of paid-in capital, currently 0.4 percent for a Yuhan Hoesa on a small-capital assumption of KRW 10,000,000, plus a 20 percent municipal surtax, with an approximate fixed minimum of KRW 60,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of incorporation and Korean legal counsel incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean law firm and Korean notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Seoul market benchmark: legal fees of KRW 2,800,000 to KRW 4,500,000, approximately USD 2,100 to USD 3,400, plus notary fees at the Korean Notary Association tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Authentication bundle for foreign certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution, articles and bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, apostille authority and Korean consulate in the origin jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille per-document official fees typically USD 10 to USD 60; consular legalization per-document fees USD 30 to USD 120; certified Korean translation fees KRW 20,000 to KRW 100,000 per page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO, PEP and sanctions screening compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a low-risk standard entity with one UBO and one foreign corporate investor; enhanced screening is required because USDC receipt and virtual concert ticketing will be subjected to virtual asset travel-rule checks.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office substance verification and address due diligence, including serviced-office or physical-site assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External corporate-services provider and Korean law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official tariff; service-provider schedule at USD 500 to USD 800 depending on whether a serviced-office lease is included and on the need for a physical inspection by Korean counsel.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: South Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 3352, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-39, governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), including Article 287-3 (contents of Articles of Incorporation), Articles 287-14 and 287-15 (capital subscription and payment), and Article 287-16 (incorporation registration); supplemental procedure under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act and the Registration of Non-Contentious Cases Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in South Korea, with electronic submission permitted through the Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under Article 287-16 of the South Korean Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under Article 287-2 of the South Korean Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation must state the amount of capital and the number of contribution units, and each member must fully pay or contribute in-kind the full value of the subscribed contribution before the incorporation registration application is filed. For a Yuhan Hoesa, no blocked escrow account, notarial verification of paid capital, or external auditor capital certificate is legally required; a bank certificate of deposit or an in-kind contribution appraisal is sufficient. The registry fee is ad valorem on the stated capital, so the USD amount shown assumes a normal small-capital formation and may vary with the actual capital amount.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the incorporation and continuing organization of KR_YUHANGHOESA, a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, is hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved.

RESOLVED, that the aggregate share capital of the company, stated as KRW [Amount] divided into [Number] contribution units with an aggregate nominal value of KRW [Amount] as set forth in the certified Articles of Incorporation, is hereby subscribed in full by the members, and each member acknowledges that the subscribed contribution has been fully paid or contributed in accordance with Article 287-14 and Article 287-15 of the Commercial Act. No unpaid contribution may be reflected in any filing, certificate, or financial record of the company, and the Representative Director is directed to complete all capital contribution formalities prior to the submission of the incorporation registration application.

RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the company is adopted and confirmed as the address identified in the Articles of Incorporation in the Republic of Korea, and the Representative Director is instructed to file the registered office address with the competent District Court Registry and to notify the National Tax Service upon business registration.

RESOLVED, that the company authorizes the opening and maintenance of corporate deposit, settlement, and payment-processing accounts at [Bank Name] and at such other financial institutions as the Representative Director deems necessary. Corporate payment systems, including Stripe and, where lawfully required or appropriate, USDC and other digital asset payment rails through a licensed virtual asset service provider, may be established only after completion of applicable customer due diligence, anti-money-laundering, and counter-financing-of-terrorism checks under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. The Representative Director, Chief Financial Officer, and one additional director shall be designated as joint signatories, with any two signatures required for transactions above KRW [Amount] and a single authorized signature for routine operating transactions.

RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed for the first statutory term: [Name] as Representative Director; [Name] as Director and Chief Financial Officer; [Name] as Director and Compliance and AML Officer; [Name] as Corporate Secretary; and [Name] as Auditor, to the extent required or otherwise appointed. The officers are vested with all authority necessary to execute and deliver formation documents, registration forms, banking mandates, leases, service agreements, tax filings, data privacy instruments, and regulatory notifications on behalf of the company.

RESOLVED, that all acts performed by the incorporators and officers prior to the date of this resolution in connection with the formation of the company are hereby ratified, and the officers are directed to complete the court registration, business registration with the National Tax Service, governance record book, data privacy policy adoption, and such further filings as are required for the lawful conduct of virtual performance hosting and digital ticket tokenization services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary public; preliminary name search through the Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage local formation counsel to verify the proposed company name KR_YUHANGHOESA in Korean and English and confirm that no same or confusingly similar entity is already registered in the same jurisdiction. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation under Article 287-3 of the Commercial Act, containing the company name, the identity of the founding members, the precise business purpose, the registered office address, the number and value of contribution units, the amount and method of capital contribution, the particulars of any non-cash contribution, the names of the directors, and the method of publication of financial statements. Circulate the draft among all members for unanimous approval, execute the Articles in front of a Korean notary public, and obtain the notarial certificate and certified copy. If the notary raises a public-policy or statutory-form objection, revise the purpose clause to narrow the activity to online digital content platform services, virtual event hosting, and digital ticketing before re-execution.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean and English
Identification cards or passports of all founding members
Power of attorney in favor of local formation counsel, if any
IROS name-search result screenshot
Notarization instructions and signed consent of all founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries a defective clause, revise the Articles and re-execute the corrected version. If the name is identified as confusingly similar, select a new Korean and English company name, update the Articles accordingly, and proceed with a fresh notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Full Payment of Subscription Capital into a Korean Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank selected by the incorporators; no government license is required for this step.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization of the Articles of Incorporation, open a provisional incorporation deposit account in the names of the incorporators or, where the bank permits, in the name of the company. Each member must transfer the full amount of the subscribed contribution in Korean won to the deposit account. For non-cash contributions, obtain a written appraisal or an affidavit signed by an independent licensed appraiser, if applicable, describing the asset and its value. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit or payment confirmation showing the company name, account number, deposit date, and amount. This certificate must be preserved in original form and attached to the incorporation registration application. There is no legal minimum capital, but the capital amount must match the Articles of Incorporation. If the bank declines the account due to incomplete beneficial ownership information, submit certified identification, source-of-funds evidence, and a corporate structure chart to satisfy the bank's financial institutions know-your-customer procedures.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Member list with contribution amounts and contribution types
Bank account application and beneficial ownership questionnaire
Source-of-funds records for each member
Non-cash contribution appraisal certificate, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the provisional account opening, submit a revised application with additional source-of-funds documentation or select another Korean commercial bank. If a member fails the bank's due diligence, replace that member before payment or obtain a legal opinion confirming the lawful source of funds and ultimate beneficial owner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, with online filing through the IROS portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fourteen calendar days after completion of the capital contribution, prepare and submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company under Article 287-16 of the Commercial Act. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of deposit or non-cash contribution appraisal, written consents of the directors and auditor to assume office, identification documents of each member and director, proof of address for the registered office, and the power of attorney if represented by counsel. Pay the court registration fee and local education surtax at the court or through the IROS electronic payment system. The court will examine the application against the Commercial Act and relevant judicial registration rules, and upon satisfaction will register the company in the commercial registry and issue a certified copy of the registration of corporate matters. The registration date is the legal date of incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company
Certified notarized copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Original bank certificate of deposit or in-kind contribution appraisal
Consent forms of directors and auditor
Identification documents of all members, directors, and auditor
Registered office consent letter or lease agreement from the property owner
Power of attorney, if applicable
Court fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a deficiency notice, use the statutory cure period to file the corrected form or document. If the court rejects the company name as confusingly similar, amend the name in the Articles and re-notarize. If the deposit certificate does not match the registered capital, deposit the shortfall and obtain a corrected certificate or file a capital reduction amendment approved by all members.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the Hometax online portal and the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty calendar days after the commencement of business operations, file the Application for Business Registration with the National Tax Service. Attach a certified copy of the corporate registration from the court registry, a corporate seal certificate, the lease or ownership certificate for the registered office, the notarized Articles of Incorporation, and identification of the representative director. Select the appropriate business category for online digital content, virtual event hosting, and digital ticketing services; do not select any manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing business code. The National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate containing the tax identification number, which is used for corporate income tax, value-added tax, withholding tax, and electronic tax invoice purposes. Register for the electronic tax invoice system and confirm the value-added tax reporting cycle at the time of application.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Application form
Certified copy of corporate registration from the District Court
Corporate seal certificate
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for the registered office
Identification of the representative director
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Electronic tax invoice registration form, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service queries the application because of a wrong business code or incomplete lease documentation, submit an amended application with a corrected business code and a revised lease or an explanatory letter describing the actual virtual concert and digital ticket revenue model. If the representative director identification issue is raised, provide a notarized Korean translation of the passport and a certified corporate authorization minute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Governance, Bank Account Activation, and Digital Payment Rail Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks; the Financial Intelligence Unit supervisory framework for digital asset payment intermediation; and the Personal Information Protection Commission for privacy governance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the final corporate banking resolution and open the active operating account. For payment rails, activate Stripe for card and digital payment processing and, if using USDC or other cryptocurrency, connect only through a licensed virtual asset service provider or through a payment processor that itself holds any required Korean license. Obtain a written legal opinion if the company's receipt of USDC is structured strictly as customer settlement and does not constitute a licenseable virtual asset services business. Adopt a privacy policy under the Personal Information Protection Act, execute data processing agreements, and implement procedures for user consent and data retention. Prepare the corporate governance book containing the minutes, the register of members, the contribution unit register, the corporate seal register, and the board resolution book. Maintain a clear audit trail for all ticket tokenization and settlement records for tax, anti-money-laundering, and consumer protection purposes. Because the company is a pure digital service provider, no industrial manufacturing permit, environmental impact assessment, or Civil Defense fire certificate is required.
required_dossiers: Corporate account opening application and board authorization mandate
Beneficial ownership and AML/KYC forms for the bank and licensed payment partners
Privacy policy and Personal Information Protection Act compliance instruments
Data processing agreements for virtual concert user data
Governance book containing the register of members, contribution unit register, board minutes, and seal register
Legal opinion or engagement letter for USDC payment flow, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or licensed virtual asset service provider rejects the USDC or cryptocurrency payment arrangement, restructure the payment flow through a different licensed processor or increase transaction monitoring and obtain a supplementary legal opinion under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. If the Personal Information Protection Commission identifies incomplete privacy disclosures, amend the privacy policy and operational consent forms before launching the virtual concert platform.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The registered business is a pure digital and consulting service comprising virtual concert hosting, online content delivery, and digital ticket tokenization; it is not classified as physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx or 52xx.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial operating permit, manufacturing license, assembly license, or warehouse license is required for the described virtual event and digital ticketing activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. The Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea has no approval or registration role for a virtual concert and digital ticket service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. The proposed activity does not fall within the project types listed under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act or its Enforcement Decree as a project requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment, Prior Environmental Review, or Environmental Registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The business does not generate wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, stationary source air emissions, or hazardous waste streams; therefore no quantitative discharge or emission standards apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. No physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility is operated, so no Civil Defense fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or occupational safety approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act is required. The company is expected to operate from an ordinary leased office or remote environment, and the building owner remains responsible for base-building fire alarm, evacuation, and general safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea; primary electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); cross-border goods clearance and export declarations are handled by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) obtains its Tax Identification Number (TIN) in the form of the Korean Business Registration Number, issued automatically by the competent District Tax Office upon incorporation under the Commercial Act and registration under the Framework Act on National Taxes. If the company has not yet registered a place of business, the legal representative must file the statutory business registration application with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the Korean address within 20 days from the date of business commencement or the first taxable event. For a foreign non-resident entity with no Korean fixed establishment, the National Tax Service requires the appointment of a domestic tax representative, filing of the statutory business registration application for a foreign business operator, submission of the foreign corporation certificate of incorporation, overseas business license/registration proof, articles or constitutional document and a notarized power of attorney, resulting in a VAT registration number embedded in the business registration certificate. Where a non-resident supplier has no Korean place of business, registration is filed with the Director of the National Tax Service through HomeTax; the foreign entity must use the same registration number for VAT invoicing, customs, and export transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or a hybrid mismatch election. A Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation per se and is taxed at entity level on its worldwide income; it cannot make pass-through elections. Hybrid mismatch rules under Korean taxation are applied as mandatory statutory adjustments rather than as electable mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service via HomeTax; export supplies and qualifying foreign-bound digital services are subject to 0% VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold denominated in Korean Won (KRW) triggers VAT registration. Any supplier of taxable goods or services in Korea, including non-resident digital service suppliers, must register from the moment of the first taxable supply. The KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover simplified taxpayer threshold for small operators is a VAT return simplification, not an exemption or registration threshold, and does not apply to a corporation or to foreign digital service suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered suppliers are required to issue a Korean tax invoice; for B2B supplies the invoice must be an electronic tax invoice transmitted to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system no later than the day after supply. The system operates via NTS-approved XML/JSON-API integration for software vendors, with no pre-clearance approval from the NTS and no anti-fraud digital stamping requirement. In parallel, B2C virtual concert and metaverse ticket sales must be recorded through the cash-receipt system when payment is made in cash or no other tax invoice is required; NTS accepts card/POS or gateway metadata as API evidence. The obligation to issue an accurate invoice under the Value Added Tax Act remains on the supplier.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export supplies, including digital services supplied to recipients outside Korea, are zero-rated under the Value Added Tax Act. A Korean LLC hosting virtual concerts and selling digital ticketing tokenization in the metaverse may zero-rate the service if the customer is a non-resident/foreign consumer and the service is actually performed or used outside Korea. Qualifying intangible/digital services recognized by the NTS include software, IT-enabled digital content, gaming, video/event streaming, audiovisual works, advertisement, and similar metaverse event services. The zero-rated supply must be evidenced by the contract, invoice, payment, and delivery arrangements; a domestic Korean ticket buyer is subject to 10% VAT on the same virtual concert supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration (Export Bill of Entry) filed through UNI-PASS for any physical goods; for pure digital virtual-concert services, a service-export declaration or the customs status record if required by Korean export procedures, showing the 0% VAT supply and foreign recipient.
Commercial invoice and Korean National Tax Service electronic tax invoice (or statutory tax invoice) annotated with the zero-rated export supply, the foreign buyer, and the service description.

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods; for virtual concert/metaverse services, the digital delivery evidence such as server access logs, virtual event platform reports, tokenized virtual ticket records, or blockchain/ledger ticketing transaction history.

Korean foreign exchange receipt certificate issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank evidencing collection of export proceeds in foreign currency; this is the Korean equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), and Korean banks do not issue an India-style FIRC.

Executed purchase/service contract, SWIFT payment credit notice, or other remittance instruction proving that the virtual event ticketing and metaverse service was supplied and paid from without Korea, with use outside Korea.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service audits zero-rated export claims and requires the complete documentation bundle to be retained by the supplier. If the 0% export VAT claim is unsupported, false, or the foreign exchange proceeds are not collected, the NTS will claw back the zero-rated input VAT previously refunded and assess 10% VAT on the entire sale amount, plus delinquency surcharges and interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent export zero-rating, including fabricated export declarations, false digital delivery logs, or fake bank receipts, subjects the company to the penalty charge of 40% of the underdeclared tax for intentional concealment, 20% for gross negligence, and possible criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; the statutory assessment/payment collection period extends to 10 years in cases of fraudulent tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and Ministry of Economy and Finance (Foreign Exchange Policy Division), with Korea Customs Service's NEDIAS foreign exchange reporting system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Korean won is largely convertible on current account transactions; remittances for dividends, royalties, and current business payments are permitted if properly reported through a licensed foreign exchange bank. However, capital account operations such as equity subscription, loans, external guarantees, and non-resident equity transfers remain subject to declaration or prior approval via the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The won is not freely convertible offshore; onshore KRW can be converted to major currencies within licensed banks, while offshore won trading is heavily restricted and mainly conducted through non-deliverable forwards. Export proceeds are required to be collected within six months from the shipping date. There is no blanket mandatory surrender ratio for export receipts; exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds in licensed foreign currency deposit accounts at domestic banks, but any settlement of domestic transactions must be executed in KRW, requiring conversion through a licensed foreign exchange bank. All transactions are captured by the NEDIAS electronic reporting platform. The key profit remittance hurdles for a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa include a statutory dividend distribution ceiling based on audited retained earnings, withholding tax at a rate of between 5% and 22% depending on the relevant tax treaty, and the need to provide a prior bank-filed foreign exchange report demonstrating that the remittance is traceable to an original capital importation certificate, foreign investment declaration, or valid trade-backed invoice. Banks may also impose additional source-of-funds scrutiny if the remittance pattern shows round-tripping or no underlying economic substance. For the virtual concert metaverse model, ticket presale revenue from foreign platforms entering through online card rails must be repatriated with clear purpose codes to avoid re-characterization as unlicensed cross-border money transfers. Overall, the regime is current-account liberalized but capital-account controlled, requiring strict documentation, reporting, and a stable onshore local banking relationship.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received within 180 days of the export declaration date; no mandatory conversion ratio is imposed, but all export foreign currency receipts must be reported through NEDIAS and either held in a licensed foreign currency account or converted to KRW through a licensed bank, with any extension of the collection period requiring prior bank approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with foreign currency deposit sub-ledger and Capital Escrow Account for shareholder remittances
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account for cross-border trade settlements
Basic Operational Currency Account for KRW operations and foreign currency account under Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Capital Escrow Account for foreign investment declaration and operational multi-currency account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Onshore fintech EMIs are not legally viable for servicing the Yuhan Hoesa because South Korea requires all foreign exchange transactions for domestic legal entities to be executed through licensed domestic deposit-taking banks operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, and the Anti-Money Laundering Act. Unlicensed offshore EMIs such as Revolut, Payoneer, and Wise cannot open KRW a/c accounts, cannot issue dollar accounts in the name of a Korean company, and cannot provide licensed FX clearing onshore. Stripe can be used only as a payment collection aggregator for the metaverse ticketing platform, but the underlying settlement must be routed through a Korean licensed acquiring bank and ultimately credited to a local Tier-1 bank operating account. Therefore, any treasury architecture that relies on a fintech EMI as the primary clearing hub is legally blocked and poses KYC underwriting rejection risk.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence of at least one statutory director and one substantial beneficial owner (or a Korean-resident authorized signatory with a power of attorney) is mandatory for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for newly incorporated Yuhan Hoesa entities. All non-resident directors and shareholders with 25% or more ownership must complete an in-person or bank-branch supervised live video KYC interview, but the final account sanctioning committee requires a local representative to attend the branch to execute the corporate resolution, specimen signatures, and authorizations. Apostilled and notarized documents are accepted as supporting evidence only, not as a substitute for physical attendance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and tax-reconciled statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (HomeTax online filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (for calendar-year entities: March 31); a one-month extension to April 30 is available upon timely application.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes (40% if the omission is fraudulent); overdue national tax accrues daily delinquency interest of 0.022%. Continued non-filing for 3 consecutive years exposes the Yuhan Hoesa to estimated assessment by the NTS and administrative strike-off of the company registration at the Commercial Registration Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Surtax Return and local tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si, Gun or Gu) of the registered office through the local ETAX portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year entities); one-month extension to April 30 aligns with the national return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% non-filing surcharge and daily delinquency interest of 0.022% apply under the Framework Act on Local Taxes; persistent delinquency can trigger compulsory collection measures, seizure of bank accounts and revocation of the ordinary place of business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return - First Half (January to June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (HomeTax online filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT non-filing surcharge of 10% of the unreported output VAT (20% for non-filing after demand); late payment interest of 0.022% per day; three consecutive filing failures may result in estimated VAT assessments and administrative strike-off for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return - Second Half (July to December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (HomeTax online filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following year for a calendar-year entity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT non-filing surcharge of 10% of the unreported output VAT (20% for non-filing after demand); late payment interest of 0.022% per day; persistent non-compliance can trigger a demand notice, estimated assessment, and deregistration of the dormant corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified CPA audit report and audited financial statements filing under the External Audit Act (if mandatory-audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service of South Korea through the DART electronic disclosure system; copy to the Securities and Futures Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the ordinary general meeting of members, to be held within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; audited statements and audit report must be transmitted to the Financial Supervisory Service within 14 days after the general meeting approval. For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the latest clearing date is April 30 if the tax-return extension is used.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply with External Audit Act reporting triggers an administrative penalty imposed by the FSS (up to KRW 50,000,000 for the company), automatic correction orders, and possible notification to the National Tax Service; when combined with tax non-filing, the registration court may administratively strike off the company after repeated official notices.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 4 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, independent certified audit is mandatory if at the preceding fiscal year-end total assets amount to at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9.2 million). The law also mandates an audit where the company is listed, where it presents consolidated financial statements under K-IFRS, or where the Financial Supervisory Commission orders an audit in the public interest. No independent headcount threshold exists for Yuhan Hoesa; however, Korean small-company exemptions expire when total assets exceed the 12-billion-won balance-sheet ceiling for two consecutive years. If the LLC grows to become the controlling parent of a group, consolidation audit rules apply under the same Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean-IFRS (K-IFRS) as endorsed by the Financial Services Commission is used for all mandatory external audits; non-mandated Yuhan Hoesa may apply Korean GAAP (General Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises) but must reconcile the statutory income statement to the Corporate Tax Adjustment Schedule for the National Tax Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a separate annual UBO return for a domestic Yuhan Hoesa. The Company must maintain a current register of members at its registered office; every transfer of a membership interest must be recorded in the register of members promptly and any necessary commercial registration amendment filed within two weeks. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a non-resident membership acquisition or transfer triggers a report to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or its designee within 30 days. Financial institutions under the Specified Financial Information Act require the ultimate beneficial owner to be confirmed at account on-boarding and refreshed at least annually during customer due diligence; therefore the Company should implement an annual UBO attestation even though no fixed government filing calendar exists.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective tax rate can be reduced through statutory tax holidays for venture startups, R&D tax credits under the Tax Incentive and Limitation Law, foreign investment zone incentives, and special intellectual-property income regimes. No dedicated metaverse free-zone holiday applies, but qualifying digital-content investments may access temporary investment tax credits and accelerated depreciation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1) and Attached Schedules under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, e-filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the return is due by March 31 of the following year, with a one-month extension available to the National Tax Service upon application; foreign corporations may obtain an additional extension if overseas financial statements are not finalized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal entity name, representative director, tax address, and entry of ultimate foreign parent ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the unique Korean business registration number assigned to the Yuhan Hoesa. For a non-resident-owned LLC, list the foreign ultimate parent and attach a power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative. Failure to register a taxable permanent establishment in Korea is an immediate red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and deductible expenses, including virtual concert ticket sales, metaverse platform service fees, and tokenized digital ticket proceeds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue sourced from Korean customers and virtual events performed in Korea. Cryptocurrency and USDC settlement amounts must be converted at the arm's-length fair market value on the transaction date. Deductions require valid third-party invoices, bank records, and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for intercompany royalties or platform fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation after applying statutory adjustments, reserves, loss carryforwards, and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean-sourced virtual performance income is taxable if attributable to a Korean permanent establishment or if the LLC is treated as a Korean domestic entity. Foreign-source income may be excluded only when no Korean PE exists and no treaty protection is abused. Transfer pricing adjustments must be made on any intercompany payment deviating from the arm's-length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, withholding tax setoff, and treaty relief declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the foreign tax credit schedule and any pending bilateral treaty relief applications. A non-resident recipient seeking reduced withholding tax must provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration. The foreign tax credit cannot exceed the Korean corporate income tax attributable to the same foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party cross-border transaction disclosure and transfer pricing documentation checklist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the International Transaction Information Report with the corporate income tax return. Disclose all royalties, ticket platform commissions, interest, and service fees paid to foreign affiliates. State whether the Local File and Master File thresholds are met and identify the tested party and profit level indicator used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax obligations on outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and non-resident service income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting dividends or royalties to a foreign parent, verify whether a DTA reduced rate is available. Statutory withholding at 20% must be withheld unless a valid Treaty Relief Application, Tax Residency Certificate, and beneficial ownership evidence are filed. Under-withholding exposes the Korean LLC to assessment, surcharges, and criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a negligence surcharge of up to 10% of the unpaid corporate income tax, which increases to 40% for false or fraudulent under-reporting. Unpaid tax accrues a daily late-payment interest surcharge. Failure to disclose international related-party transactions triggers additional transfer pricing penalties, and criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment or fines up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% statutory withholding on outbound dividends, plus 2% local income tax surtax, producing an aggregate 22% before treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must submit a Tax Treaty Relief Application to the Korean National Tax Service, attach a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty jurisdiction, provide a beneficial ownership declaration, demonstrate that the income is not attributable to a Korean permanent establishment, and receive approval before payment or file for refund through HomeTax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic withholding on royalties and intercompany interest is 20%, plus 2% local income tax surtax. Under most Korean bilateral DTA networks, the treaty rate is reduced to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is triggered when annual gross revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transaction value exceeds KRW 5 billion. The International Transaction Information Report must be filed with the annual corporate tax return for material related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation, but the Korean tax authorities apply substance-over-form and OECD BEPS principles. A non-resident virtual concert operator must demonstrate that Core Income-Generating Activities are performed in Korea if claiming a permanent establishment or seeking treaty benefits. Artificial offshore arrangements lacking local employees, offices, and real operational control will be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting virtual concert ticket revenue by diverting ticket proceeds from Korean customers to a foreign shell entity or cryptocurrency wallet while retaining economic risk in the Korean LLC and failing to file the statutory corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to 3 times the amount evaded. The Korean National Tax Service also imposes a 40% fraudulent under-reporting penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced when the LLC is an alter ego of its directors. Directors are personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties, face civil asset restitution, are subject to NTS blacklisting and travel bans, and may receive criminal imprisonment for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean LLC with no physical office, no local employees, and no substantive economic activity while interposing a non-resident affiliate in a treaty jurisdiction solely to divert digital ticket royalties, dividends, and platform service fees to obtain reduced DTA rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service may deny treaty benefits, recharacterize the intercompany transaction, and impose transfer pricing penalties of up to 20% of the adjusted income. Abusive tax avoidance also triggers a 40% penalty on the resulting under-reported tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly structure the shell arrangement can be held jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency. Piercing the corporate veil permits seizure of personal assets, criminal fraud prosecution, director disqualification, and inclusion on the NTS compliance blacklist with travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Foreign Exchange Reporting Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC cryptocurrency and Stripe settlement payments for virtual concert tickets without implementing customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, or required foreign exchange declarations, and settling through unregistered overseas wallet accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Transaction Reports Act, failure to report suspicious virtual-asset transactions carries criminal liability of up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine up to KRW 50 million. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, unreported outbound transfers may be penalized up to 20% of the unreported amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize crypto settlement or offshore remittances may be prosecuted as accomplices, subject to personal asset forfeiture, passport revocation and travel bans, and permanent debarment from acting as corporate directors in Korea.
